Regression on Predicted Categories with Calibrated Class Probabilities

Source: R/soft_lm.R
soft_lm.Rd

Estimates the partial association between a latent categorical group and an outcome when the group is not observed, but a classifier supplies calibrated class probabilities for every observation. It replaces the common practice of regressing the outcome on the predicted label (argmax or a confidence threshold), which distorts the estimate (for a binary group it typically attenuates it) and can give confidence intervals whose coverage is far below the nominal level.

Usage

soft_lm(
  formula,
  probs,
  data,
  reference = 1L,
  learner = lrn_ranger(),
  folds = 5L,
  n_rep = 1L,
  weights = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

[mandatory] (formula) A two-sided formula outcome ~ controls. The right-hand side lists the controls; their functional form is left to the learner. Matrix-valued terms such as poly(x, 2) enter as one control per column. Use outcome ~ 1 for no controls.

probs

[mandatory] (matrix, data.frame, character, formula or numeric) Class probabilities, one column per category and rows summing to one: a matrix or data frame, a character vector of column names in data, a one-sided formula such as ~ p_a + p_b + p_c, or, for a binary group, a numeric vector of probabilities of the second category, in which case the categories are named "0" and "1". A prefix shared by all column names (such as prob_ or .pred_) is removed to obtain category labels.

data

[mandatory] (data.frame) A data frame containing the outcome and the controls.

reference

[optional] (character or integer) The reference category, by name or position (default: 1, the first column of probs).

learner

[optional] (softcats_learner or list) A learner (see learners) used for both nuisances, or a list list(m = , r = ) with separate learners for the outcome regression and the score regressions (default: lrn_ranger()).

folds

[optional] (integer) Number of cross-fitting folds, at least two (default: 5).

n_rep

[optional] (integer) Number of repetitions of cross-fitting with new fold splits (default: 1).

weights

[optional] (numeric, character or formula) Non-negative observation weights, for example survey weights: a numeric vector, a column name of data or a one-sided formula (default: NULL).

cluster

[optional] (vector, character or formula) Cluster identifier for cluster-robust standard errors: a vector, a column name of data or a one-sided formula (default: NULL).

seed

[optional] (integer) Seed for the fold splits and stochastic learners. The random number generator state of the session is restored afterwards (default: NULL).

Value

An object of class softcats, with methods for print(), summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), nobs(), residuals(), fitted(), formula(), plot(), generics::tidy() and generics::glance(). It works with update(), broom, modelsummary and lmtest::coeftest().

Model

For a latent group \(G\) with categories \(1, \dots, K\) (category 1 is the reference) and class probabilities, or scores, \(p\), the target is \(\tau\) in the partially linear model $$E[Y \mid G, X] = \mu(X) + \sum_{k = 2}^{K} \tau_k 1\{G = k\},$$ where \(\mu\) is unrestricted. The probabilities must be calibrated conditionally on the controls, \(E[1\{G = k\} \mid p, X] = p_k\). Under this condition and the exclusion condition \(E[Y \mid G, p, X] = E[Y \mid G, X]\) (see Requirements), with \(a = p - E[p \mid X]\) (reference column removed) and \(m(X) = E[Y \mid X]\), $$E[a\,(Y - m(X))] = E[a a^\top]\,\tau ,$$ so \(\tau\) is identified from the unlabelled data whenever the scores vary beyond what the controls explain, that is, whenever \(E[a a^\top]\) is non-singular. For two categories, \(E[a a^\top]\) is the residual score variance \(V^* = E[\mathrm{Var}(p \mid X)]\).

Estimation and inference

The nuisances \(m(X)\) and \(E[p_k \mid X]\) are estimated by cross-fitting with the chosen learner. The estimator solves the sample version of the moment equation above, whose estimating function is Neyman-orthogonal in both nuisances. This is the partialling-out estimator of Robinson (1988), with cross-fitted nuisance estimates and the probabilities as regressors. Without weights or clusters, the estimate is asymptotically normal with variance \(M^{-1} E[u^2 a a^\top] M^{-1} / n\), \(M = E[a a^\top]\) and \(u = Y - m(X) - a^\top\tau\), when both nuisance estimates are consistent, their errors satisfy \(\|\hat m - m\|_2 \|\hat r - r\|_2 + \|\hat r - r\|_2^2 = o_P(n^{-1/2})\) and further regularity conditions hold (Chernozhukov et al. 2018; Kurbucz 2026, arXiv:2608.11784). Standard errors are sandwich estimates, heteroskedasticity-robust (HC0) by default and cluster-robust (CR1, with the factor \(G / (G - 1)\) for \(G\) clusters) when cluster is supplied. With cluster, folds are formed from whole clusters. With n_rep > 1, cross-fitting is repeated with new fold splits; estimates are averaged and the variance includes the spread across splits. With random forests, several splits (for example n_rep = 5) are advisable, because in simulations the variance from a single split understates the variability of the estimate.

Requirements

The classifier must use information beyond the controls (classifier features that are not in formula), otherwise the scores are a function of the controls and the effect is not identified; score_spectrum() reports how much information is left. These extra features must not affect the outcome directly; exclusion_test() checks this on labelled data. Conditional calibration can be checked with calibration_check() and repaired on labelled data with recalibrate(), and drift_sensitivity() bounds the bias from calibration error. The estimand is a partial association, not a causal effect.

References

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). Coarsening latent-class probabilities: Directional distortion and coverage loss. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.11784

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). When to trust confidence thresholding: Calibration diagnostics for pseudo-labelled regression. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2605.12780

Chernozhukov, V., Chetverikov, D., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., Hansen, C., Newey, W. and Robins, J. (2018). Double/debiased machine learning for treatment and structural parameters. The Econometrics Journal, 21(1), C1–C68. doi:10.1111/ectj.12097

Robinson, P. M. (1988). Root-N-consistent semiparametric regression. Econometrica, 56(4), 931–954. doi:10.2307/1912705

See also

compare_hard() for the cost of using predicted labels instead, soft_check() for a one-page diagnostic report.

Examples

# Example: Three categories, probabilities given as column names
d <- sim_softcats(n = 2000, K = 3, seed = 1)
fit <- soft_lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = c("prob_A", "prob_B", "prob_C"),
               data = d, learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 1)
fit
#> Regression on predicted categories (calibrated soft labels)
#> 
#> Call:
#> soft_lm(formula = y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = c("prob_A", "prob_B", 
#>     "prob_C"), data = d, learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 1)
#> 
#> Difference from reference category 'A':
#>   Estimate Std. Error   2.5 %  97.5 %
#> B   0.9715     0.1355  0.7059  1.2370
#> C  -0.6301     0.1362 -0.8971 -0.3632
#> 
#> Observations: 2000   Cross-fitting: 5 folds, 1 split
#> Learner: lm (degree 3)
summary(fit)
#> Regression on predicted categories (calibrated soft labels)
#> 
#> Call:
#> soft_lm(formula = y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = c("prob_A", "prob_B", 
#>     "prob_C"), data = d, learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 1)
#> 
#> Reference category: A   Categories: A, B, C
#> Observations: 2000
#> Cross-fitting: 5 folds, 1 split   Learner: lm (degree 3)
#> Standard errors: heteroskedasticity-robust (HC0)
#> 
#>   Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> B   0.9715     0.1355   7.169 7.55e-13 ***
#> C  -0.6301     0.1362  -4.627 3.71e-06 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Score information beyond the controls
#>   Share of score variance not explained by the controls: 0.956, 0.881
#>   Condition number of E[aa']: 11.7
confint(fit)
#>        2.5 %     97.5 %
#> B  0.7059052  1.2371067
#> C -0.8970609 -0.3632156
attr(d, "tau")
#>    B    C 
#>  1.0 -0.5 

# Example: Binary group, probability of the second category as a vector
b <- sim_softcats(n = 2000, K = 2, seed = 2)
soft_lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = b$prob_B, data = b,
        learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 2)
#> Regression on predicted categories (calibrated soft labels)
#> 
#> Call:
#> soft_lm(formula = y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = b$prob_B, data = b, 
#>     learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 2)
#> 
#> Difference from reference category '0':
#>   Estimate Std. Error  2.5 % 97.5 %
#> 1    1.028    0.07601 0.8788  1.177
#> 
#> Observations: 2000   Cross-fitting: 5 folds, 1 split
#> Learner: lm (degree 3)
